note: A society-history blog post, quoting Stephen Longstreet's Chicago and The Chronicle of Catherine Eddy Beveridge (2005), Delia Caton's niece's diary of 1902-1908. It says Field's first marriage was unhappy ('Mrs. Field led Marshall Field a hell-on-earth life', Longstreet), that Delia was the daughter of a founder of Hibbard, Spencer & Bartlett and the wife of Arthur J. Caton, son of Judge John Dean Caton; that there were rumours they were lovers for nearly 30 years; that, per the Chronicle, the relationship 'was so intimate that the existence of a subterranean tunnel connecting their homes was rumored'; that 'Delia sometimes traveled to Europe with Marshall Field without Arthur accompanying them'; that Nannie Field died in France in 1896; that Arthur Caton died 'November 18, 1904, at New York's Waldorf-Astoria hotel', the cause inexact, 'Some said he succumbed to liver failure. Others ascribed the demise to peritonitis', and that an Ottawa, Illinois Times story suggested suicide. Gossip it reports is reported as gossip.
what_it_supplies: Arthur Caton's death, 18 November 1904, at the Waldorf-Astoria, and the disputed cause
the tunnel rumour and the Europe travel, as the Beveridge Chronicle reports them
the Fields' unhappy marriage, as Longstreet tells it
what_it_does_not_supply: any date of the Field-Caton marriage
